clue.text: Touchstone's courteous vessel

definitions.meaning: Touchstone, the clown in Shakespeare's As You Like It, lists the degrees of a quarrel
a glass flask with a long bent neck used for distilling

explanation.surface: A clown's polite piece of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both Touchstone's polite reply in As You Like It and a distilling flask used in laboratories.

clue.text: Like the last angle of the space capsule ?

definitions.text: Like the last angle of the space capsule ?

parts.words: Like the last angle of the space capsule ?
parts.note: a capsule coming back into the atmosphere makes its final approach at an angle; an angle pointing inwards in geometry has the same descriptive word

explanation.surface: The final approach angle of a spacecraft returning to Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: A geometric term for an inward-pointing angle doubles as 'coming back in', like a capsule returning to Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes an angle pointing inwards, and also something entering again, like a returning capsule.

clue.text: A dog of a soldier

definitions.meaning: a small breed bred to dig after foxes and badgers
Slang for a member of the British Territorial Army, the part-time reserve

explanation.surface: A soldier described as a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a small breed of hunting hound and slang for a part-time Territorial Army volunteer.

clue.text: Is golf one of them ?

parts.note: golf is played in rounds, but the phrase meant names party games, often cards, for any number of players with no partnerships

explanation.surface: A question about whether golf belongs to some category of sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf is played over rounds, so the question invites a yes; the term really means parlour or card games for many players.
explanation.definitionFit: Party and card games played by any number, each for themselves, carry this name; golf is played in rounds too.

clue.text: It's the way I'm chased by headless Zulus that spurs me on

indicators.note: one thing chased by another comes before it, so the pieces after follow in order

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a common crossword way
taken as written

indicators.note: headless means the opening letter of the word Zulus is cut off

parts.note: taken as the word itself, before losing its head

explanation.surface: A rider urged on by a band of warriors pursuing him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' cuts the Z from the Zulus; 'chased by' means the trimmed warriors come after the way and 'I'm'. 'spurs' looks like a rider's spurs but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulus is anything that rouses or goads someone into action.

clue.text: Slow movers go to hell for their protection

definitions.text: Slow movers go to hell for their protection

parts.words: Slow movers go to hell for their protection
parts.note: slow shelled creatures retreat into their shells for safety; read 'hell' with the S of 'movers' run on to hear 'shell'

explanation.surface: Sluggards head for damnation to stay safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'movers' runs on to make 'go to (s)hell': the slow animals pull into their shells.
explanation.definitionFit: These slow reptiles carry a hard shell to retreat into for protection.

clue.text: Low purpose

definitions.meaning: to intend, as in 'I purpose to go'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means base or ignoble, and as a verb to intend or have in mind.

clue.text: Time to stand and stare — and repent perhaps

definitions.meaning: W. H. Davies's poem with this title asks what life is if we have no time to stand and stare
from the saying 'marry in haste, repent at' this word

explanation.surface: A pause to gaze, and maybe to regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time is the theme of Davies's poem and the moment in the proverb when hasty marriers regret their choice.

clue.text: Horse becomes waterlogged when surrounded by sauce

indicators.note: says the horse sits inside the sauce

parts.note: soy sauce, the salty Chinese condiment
gee-gee, written GG, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A horse drenched in gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: Soggy means soaked through and heavy with moisture.

clue.text: Dire Doctor Hill

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means cruel or deadly
the Doctor of the rhyme 'I do not like thee, Doctor' of this name
an upland hill in northern England

explanation.surface: A terrible physician on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: deadly, the disliked doctor of the old rhyme, and a moorland hill in the Lake District.

clue.text: On the way to make one true

indicators.note: the letters of 'one true' are used to make a new arrangement, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Travelling towards turning a single thing genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' signals rearranging the seven letters of ONE TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase means while travelling, along the road towards a destination.

clue.text: University is for studying

definitions.meaning: the University of ..., in the Berkshire town west of London
perusing books, being a student of a subject

explanation.surface: A student's life summed up as being all about study.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a British university town and the act of perusing books or studying a subject, as in 'reading law'.

clue.text: Its back passing is playful

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Its back passing is playful' (5,5) gives no parse for THIRD FLOOR; neither the scan nor a reprint shows other words, so the printed clue or answer looks wrong

clue.text: Landing on the typewriter, we hear

indicators.note: says the word for a typewriter button is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: each letter on a typewriter is struck on a key

explanation.surface: Something touching down on a typing machine, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing' looks like an arrival but is a noun: a harbour landing place.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a stone wharf where boats land passengers and goods.

clue.text: Lack of agreement with leading girl's team

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Lack of agreement with leading girl's team' (10): DI'S + SIDE gives DISSIDE but no word in 'with leading' yields the remaining NCE; no parse found
annotationWithheld.clue: Lack of agreement with leading girl's team

clue.text: A railway point must be level

parts.note: BR stood for British Rail, the former national railway
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Points on a railway line must sit flush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like railway points (a junction), but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things side by side, keeping pace with each other, are level.

clue.text: Just the bird to make lace-the honours are even

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
for, as in 'just the thing for the job'
to tat is to make lace by knotting thread

explanation.surface: The perfect bird for lace-making, and the score is level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the bird to make lace' reads as 'exactly the tit for tatting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaliation in kind leaves both sides square, with neither ahead.

clue.text: Money that boxers may get

definitions.meaning: old slang for coins, especially gold sovereigns
a shiner is a black eye, a common boxing injury

explanation.surface: Prize money and bruises are both a fighter's reward.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for shining coins and also for black eyes picked up in the ring.

clue.text: A brace of Americans ?

parts.note: a brace looks like a pair of people, but Americans call trouser braces by another name, so this is one of those straps

explanation.surface: Two people from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brace' looks like a pair; it is a trouser strap, which Americans call by another name.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English, suspenders are the straps British speakers call braces.

clue.text: Hill cleft by rushing water

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in south-west England
a rent is a split or cleft

explanation.surface: A hillside split open by a stream in spate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleft by' reads as one piece cut into another, but the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent, fast-flowing stream.

clue.text: Do a turn perhaps in building

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of 'Do a turn' may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perform a routine, maybe, inside a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, usually domed.

clue.text: Alien agreement to hides for birds

parts.note: si is yes in Spanish or Italian, a foreign way to agree
animal hides are skins

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial consents to giving pelts to some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Siskins are small yellow-green finches.

clue.text: Rising soldier, having won his spurs we hear, is fired

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the soldier is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: says the words for being dubbed are to be spoken, giving the same sound with other letters

parts.note: a knight won his spurs, so having won them means having been dubbed a knight

explanation.surface: A soldier is promoted, earns his knighthood, and is then sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns GI into IG. 'fired' looks like dismissed but means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ignited has been set on fire.

clue.text: "Like, give his little senate laws ' (Pope)

parts.note: a line from Pope's Epistle to Dr Arbuthnot, about Addison presiding over his circle, with the name of a Roman statesman left blank

explanation.surface: A quotation from Alexander Pope with one name missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash after 'Like' for the missing name; fill it from Pope's portrait of Addison as Atticus.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope compares Addison to the stern Roman senator Marcus Porcius, who laid down the law to his fellow senators.

clue.text: Dry nut of a police artist

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
RA, Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A dull eccentric among police painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is the dried kernel of the coconut, pressed for oil.

clue.text: With which one plays the ace of trumps-some trick!

definitions.text: With which one plays the ace of trumps-some trick!

parts.words: With which one plays the ace of trumps-some trick!
parts.note: reads like a card play, but it describes the swindle in which a trickster wins a victim's trust by bluff

explanation.surface: A card player's flourish in leading the top trump.
explanation.walkthrough: The card language misleads: the 'trick' is a swindle, and what is played is assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler plays on self-assurance and trust, hence the confidence trick.

clue.text: Deaf to what ex-Army types do ?

indicators.note: to, as in 'turned to', signals that the letters of 'Deaf' change into another word

explanation.surface: An old soldier who can't hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The song says old soldiers never die, they simply fade away. 'to' rearranges DEAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Old soldiers dwindle and slip quietly from view, as the barrack-room song says.

clue.text: The French degree for a monk

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine
MA, Master of Arts, a university degree

explanation.surface: A French qualification for a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk.

clue.text: It's a hanging, matter

parts.note: reads like a capital crime, but describes an ornament that hangs from a necklace

explanation.surface: A crime that carries the death sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a hanging matter' suggests the gallows; the thing meant simply hangs, as jewellery does.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is a piece of jewellery hanging on a chain.

clue.text: Not deed indicated

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed (scan) is 'Not indeed indicated': NOT inside DEED needs 'indeed' split as 'in deed', so the one word is both the container indicator and the fodder DEED

clue.text: It took three apples to tempt this woman

definitions.text: It took three apples to tempt this woman

parts.words: It took three apples to tempt this woman
parts.note: the Greek huntress who raced her suitors; Hippomenes dropped three golden apples to win the race and her hand

explanation.surface: A temptress story recalling Eve, but with three apples.
explanation.walkthrough: The apples suggest Eve, but Eve needed only one; the three golden apples belong to a Greek myth about a foot race.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the swift runner stopped to pick up three golden apples and so lost the race to Hippomenes.

clue.text: Swamp the German used to keep things off

parts.note: a fen is a marsh or swamp, as in the East Anglian Fens
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German bog put to use as a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A fender is a guard, such as a fireplace screen or a boat's bumper, that keeps things away.
